en.p: There are a circle with diameter $\mathrm{AB}$ of length $10$ and a point $\mathrm{C}$ on segment $\mathrm{AB}$ with $\overline{\mathrm{AC}}=4$. Take point $\mathrm{P}$ on this circle so that $\angle\mathrm{PCB}=\theta$, and let $\mathrm{Q}$ be the point, other than $\mathrm{P}$, where the line through $\mathrm{P}$ perpendicular to segment $\mathrm{AB}$ meets this circle. If $S(\theta)$ is the area of triangle $\mathrm{PCQ}$, find the value of $-7\times S'\!\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)$. (Given that $0<\theta<\dfrac{\pi}{2}$.) [4 points]
